> But is there an way to get the combined result as I wanted in the last
> line [All i need is output like this] and also is there any way to
> visualize these ?

One way to visualize correlations is a series of scatterplots. You can
generate them all at once with ggplot with facet_wrap, using the
reshape package to prepare your data.

fmelted <- melt(f, id=c("samples", "ptbgene"))
ggplot(fmelted, aes(x=ptbgene, y=value)) + geom_point() +
geom_smooth() + facet_wrap(~ variable)

You might be able to compute the correlations using the same principle
("melting" the data set and playing with aggregate or with the plyr
package).

Gaël

Check out the ezCor function in the ez package; it's basically a
wrapper around a bunch of ggplot code to visualize a correlation
matrix. The result is a modifiable ggplot object.
